key_insight: SolarChain-Eval shows that in decentralized energy markets, higher reward can come at the cost of physical safety unless agents are constrained by explicit physics and audited interventions.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark provides a practical way to evaluate autonomous market-control agents on both economic performance and cyber-physical trustworthiness, not just profit.
method: Gymnasium-compatible MDP for hourly market governance decisions
Multi-objective evaluation: utility, safety, slippage, smoothness, fairness, and auditability
LLM Planner/Auditor layer adds action bounds, high-risk reviews, and structured intervention logs
evidence_signal: Experiments across static, random, myopic, RL, and RL+LLM policies exposed a utility-safety trade-off, and removing physics penalties let agents exploit invalid generation and artificial liquidity.
watch_item: The LLM Planner/Auditor improves transparency and mitigates some risks, but it cannot fully fix a misspecified reward or replace hard physical constraints.
paper_title: SolarChain-Eval: A Physics-Constrained Benchmark for Trustworthy Economic Agents in Decentralized Energy Markets
